candidates.why: Line 2016 stores `_obj->encr_sat_data[i] = (char*)dest.chain`, i.e. a raw alias into the `dest` Bit_Chain buffer. `dest` is later freed by `bit_chain_free (&dest)` at line 2276 (which frees dest.chain at bits.c:3032). The aliased pointers in encr_sat_data[] are then read at line 2339 (`dwg_encrypt_SAT1(..., _obj->encr_sat_data[i], ...)`) and line 2350, and freed again at line 2342 — use-after-free of the freed dest buffer.

The alias stored at line 2016 points into dest.chain, but dest.chain is realloc'd by bit_chain_alloc (bits.c:3015) at many later points (e.g. lines 2079, 2099, 2138, 2155, 2167, 2178, 2195, 2222). realloc may move the buffer, leaving encr_sat_data[i] dangling; it is then dereferenced at line 2339/2350. (Stale-pointer variant of the same aliasing bug.)

On the error path at line 2073 `bit_chain_free (&dest)` is called and the function returns at 2076, so that path is fine; but the same `dest` is also freed at 2093 and 2276. Worth flagging because `dest` is a stack Bit_Chain whose chain is aliased into _obj->encr_sat_data (line 2016) — the free at 2276 invalidates those aliases (see the 2276/2339 entry).

Line 752 does `Bit_Chain dat1 = *hdl_dat;` (shallow copy, dat1.chain == hdl_dat->chain). Line 759 `bit_chain_free (&dat1)` frees that shared chain and sets dat1.chain=NULL. Line 761 then does `*hdl_dat = *dat;` overwriting hdl_dat, so hdl_dat->chain becomes dat->chain — no direct UAF, but any other alias of the old hdl_dat->chain (e.g. obj_flush_hdlstream at 758 stored pointers) would dangle. Flagging as suspicious aliasing.

`bit_chain_free (&sec_dat[type])` at line 3133 frees the section chain inside the per-section loop; the loop at 3065-3135 iterates over stream_order and re-reads `sec_dat[type].size`/`.chain` (lines 3074, 3083, 3111, 3121, 3129) for each type. If the same `type` appears again in stream_order after being freed, sec_dat[type].chain is NULL (set at bits.c:3033) so it is guarded at 3083 — but the free-then-reuse pattern across iterations is worth flagging.

`bit_chain_free (&file_dat)` at line 3168 frees file_dat.chain; line 3170 then logs `dat->chain[0x80]` — but `dat` was restored to orig_dat at 3165, so this reads the original chain, not file_dat. Not a UAF, but the free at 3168 immediately followed by reads of a chain that was just copied from file_dat (via decrypt_R2004_header at 3166) is a fragile pattern worth noting.

bit_chain_free (3032) frees dat->chain and NULLs it (3033), but bit_chain_alloc at 3014-3015 assigns `dat->chain = realloc(dat->chain, ...)` and only checks `!dat->chain` at 3016 after the assignment — on realloc failure the original pointer is lost (leak), and callers that hold a second alias of the old chain (e.g. out_dxf.c:2016) are left dangling. Cross-function aliasing hazard.

bit_chain_init_dat (2996) calls bit_chain_init which does `dat->chain = calloc(...)` at 2980, overwriting any existing dat->chain without freeing it. Callers in encode.c (2104, 2144, 2183, 2398, 2614) pass elements of the uninitialized stack array `sec_dat[]` (declared at encode.c:1770) — reading/overwriting an uninitialized pointer field. Leak / garbage-pointer hazard rather than clean UAF.
